translationRepairs: Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Bin, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.

Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Fu, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
Focus unit lists 丹、延、鄜、坊; 鄜 is Fuzhou (Fu), distinct from 邠 (Bin) in s0009 and s0012. The idiomatic wrongly renders 鄜 as Bin; Fu restores the toponym.
Once Bin and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
Once Fu and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
太祖已下鄜、坊 names Fu and Fang as already taken; 邠州 appears only as the next target in 復攻邠州. Replacing the first Bin with Fu corrects the place already held without changing the Bin campaign order.
Li Keyong brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
The Prince of Jin brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
Chinese has 晉王, not a personal name. The prior idiomatic invents Li Keyong; after Hui’s surrender in s0049 and before 莊宗立 in s0051, 晉王 is Li Cunxu. “The Prince of Jin” matches the source wording.
Li Keyong made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
The Prince of Jin made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
Focus unit opens 晉王拜寶; the idiomatic wrongly names Li Keyong. Adjacent s0080’s 莊宗 shows this is Li Cunxu’s Jin court. “The Prince of Jin” restores the title actually written.
Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Cao, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Jun;
Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Chan, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Yun;
Chinese 分相、澶、衞 has 澶 (Chan), not 曹 (Cao), and 以張筠為節度使: 筠 is Yun, not Jun. Both proposed corrections match the characters; the rest of the sentence can stand.
